subject: Numeracy
title: Show what we know again
objectives: Children will show Term 2 learning through play stations.
Teachers will gather evidence for every child’s Term 2 record.
content: Revising Term 2 learning through play stations and gathering evidence for the Term 2 record.
teachingActivities: Keep stations relaxed; observe quietly; give help only when asked; praise effort and kindness.
learnerActivities: Revisit familiar games, play with a friend and show what they know in many ways.
resources: Materials from Weeks 1 to 9 of Term 2
assessment: Use the term record to judge each strand: comparing quantity, counting to five, numerals, measures, patterns and shapes. Use two or more occasions before recording Secure.
expectedOutcomes: Completes familiar tasks with growing independence.
Each child has an observation record for Term 2.
crossCurricular: Literacy: songs and rhymes from the term
Social Habits: working with a friend and tidying up

lessons.title: Counting and numeral games
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will revisit counting to five and numerals 1 to 5 through games.
successCriteria: Counts up to five objects by touching
Matches numerals 1 to 5 to groups with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have met counting to five, numerals 1 to 5, long and short, heavy and light, patterns, squares and triangles.
lessons.starter: Beat the drum five times and say "One, two, three, four, five." Say "Let us play our counting games."
teacherActivities: Play "Count the blocks" with a tray of up to five blocks.
Play "Show me the numeral" with cards 1 to 5.
Play "Fill the tray": show a numeral and ask children to count out that many blocks.
Sing the rhyme to five with finger actions.
learnerActivities: Children touch and count the blocks.
Children point to the numeral called.
Child counts blocks to match the numeral.
Children sing and show fingers.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Play "Count the blocks" with a tray of up to five blocks. Children: Children touch and count the blocks.
Step 2. Teacher: Play "Show me the numeral" with cards 1 to 5. Children: Children point to the numeral called.
Step 3. Teacher: Play "Fill the tray": show a numeral and ask children to count out that many blocks. Children: Child counts blocks to match the numeral.
Step 4. Teacher: Sing the rhyme to five with finger actions. Children: Children sing and show fingers.

practical.title: Counting stations
steps: Set up counting and numeral stations.
practical.safety: Use large blocks only; supervise stations; keep cards on the mat.

differentiation.support: Count only to three and use numerals 1 to 3.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to count to five and write or trace the numeral.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many blocks?
questions.expected: The correct number up to five.

questions.question: Which numeral goes with this group?

lessons.conclusion: Sing the counting rhyme and tidy up together.
lessons.homeConnection: Count to five at home with real objects.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit counting to five and numerals 1 to 5 through games" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Comparing games
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will revisit more and same, long and short, and heavy and light through games.
successCriteria: Chooses the longer or heavier object
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have met counting to five, numerals 1 to 5, long and short, heavy and light, patterns, squares and triangles.
lessons.starter: Say "Today we play games about more, long and heavy. Show me what you know!" Show a big and a small pile of blocks.
teacherActivities: Show two piles of blocks and ask "Which has more?"
Show two ropes and ask "Which is longer?" Line up the ends.
Show the two baskets and ask "Which is heavy?"
Let children play with a friend at each game.
learnerActivities: Children point to the pile with more.
Children point to the longer rope.
Children lift and point to the heavy basket.
Pairs play and take turns to ask each other.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show two piles of blocks and ask "Which has more?" Children: Children point to the pile with more.
Step 2. Teacher: Show two ropes and ask "Which is longer?" Line up the ends. Children: Children point to the longer rope.
Step 3. Teacher: Show the two baskets and ask "Which is heavy?" Children: Children lift and point to the heavy basket.
Step 4. Teacher: Let children play with a friend at each game. Children: Pairs play and take turns to ask each other.

practical.title: Comparing stations
practical.safety: Use soft ropes and light objects; keep weights moderate; supervise stations.

differentiation.support: Use only one comparison game at a time.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to ask a friend questions such as "Which is longer?"

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Sing the long and short song and tidy up together.
lessons.homeConnection: Compare things at home: which is heavier, longer, has more.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit more and same, long and short, and heavy and light through games" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Pattern and shape games
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will revisit patterns and the shapes circle, square and triangle through games.
successCriteria: Names or points to circle, square and triangle
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have met counting to five, numerals 1 to 5, long and short, heavy and light, patterns, squares and triangles.
lessons.starter: Beat a clap and stamp pattern and say "What comes next?" Show the three shapes and say "Let us play pattern and shape games."
teacherActivities: Play the clap and stamp pattern and ask children to continue it.
Make a red and blue block pattern and ask for the next block.
Show the shapes and ask "Find the triangle" and "Find the square."
Make a shape pattern: circle, square, circle, square.
learnerActivities: Children clap and stamp in the pattern.
Child places the next block.
Children find and name the shapes.
Children continue the shape pattern with support.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Play the clap and stamp pattern and ask children to continue it. Children: Children clap and stamp in the pattern.
Step 2. Teacher: Make a red and blue block pattern and ask for the next block. Children: Child places the next block.
Step 3. Teacher: Show the shapes and ask "Find the triangle" and "Find the square." Children: Children find and name the shapes.
Step 4. Teacher: Make a shape pattern: circle, square, circle, square. Children: Children continue the shape pattern with support.

practical.title: Pattern and shape stations
steps: Set up a pattern station and a shape station.
Children visit each with a friend.
practical.safety: Use large cardboard shapes; supervise stations; keep the floor clear.

differentiation.support: Offer only one pattern and one shape at a time.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make their own shape pattern.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What comes next in this pattern?
questions.expected: The next item in the pattern.

lessons.conclusion: Sing the shape songs and tidy up together.
lessons.homeConnection: Make shape patterns with cut-out paper at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit patterns and the shapes circle, square and triangle through games" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Market counting game
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will use counting to five, more and same, and shapes in a pretend market.
successCriteria: Counts out up to five items
Uses more or same in play
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have met counting to five, numerals 1 to 5, long and short, heavy and light, patterns, squares and triangles.
lessons.starter: Set up the market and say "The market is open! Who wants to buy three oranges?" Show a number card.
teacherActivities: Act as a trader. Ask a child to buy the number of items on a card.
Ask "Who has more? Who has the same?" after two children buy.
Ask "Find a round fruit" and "Find a square box."
Swap roles so each child is the trader and the customer.
learnerActivities: Child counts out the items and puts them in a basket.
Children compare baskets and say more or same.
Children find shapes in the market.
Children take turns to sell and buy.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Act as a trader. Ask a child to buy the number of items on a card. Children: Child counts out the items and puts them in a basket.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Who has more? Who has the same?" after two children buy. Children: Children compare baskets and say more or same.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "Find a round fruit" and "Find a square box." Children: Children find shapes in the market.
Step 4. Teacher: Swap roles so each child is the trader and the customer. Children: Children take turns to sell and buy.

practical.title: Number market
steps: Give each customer a number card.
They count out that number of items.
practical.safety: Use toy items only; keep baskets on the table; supervise role play.

differentiation.support: Use number cards 1 to 3 and ask for one item at a time.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to buy five items and say how many they have.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many oranges did you buy?

lessons.conclusion: Close the market and say "Thank you, goodbye."
lessons.homeConnection: Play shopping at home and count out items to a family member.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "use counting to five, more and same, and shapes in a pretend market" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Show and celebrate again
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will show Term 2 learning in familiar games and celebrate their work.
successCriteria: Takes part confidently in at least three familiar tasks
Shows or says one thing they have learned
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have met counting to five, numerals 1 to 5, long and short, heavy and light, patterns, squares and triangles.
lessons.starter: Sing a favourite song from the term. Say "Today we show what we know and celebrate."
teacherActivities: Set up six quick stations: more and same, counting, numerals, length and weight, patterns, shapes. Spend three minutes at each.
At each station ask a simple question and wait.
Take photographs of each child at work and record levels.
Give each child a sticker or certificate and say one thing they did well.
learnerActivities: Children visit stations in pairs.
Child answers or shows the response.
Children continue playing.
Children receive their award and clap for friends.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up six quick stations: more and same, counting, numerals, length and weight, patterns, shapes. Spend three minutes at each. Children: Children visit stations in pairs.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask a simple question and wait. Children: Child answers or shows the response.
Step 3. Teacher: Take photographs of each child at work and record levels. Children: Children continue playing.
Step 4. Teacher: Give each child a sticker or certificate and say one thing they did well. Children: Children receive their award and clap for friends.

practical.title: Celebration stations
steps: Children visit each with a friend.
Teacher records evidence and takes photos.
practical.safety: Remove small items; supervise all stations; never compare children aloud.

differentiation.support: Visit only three stations, with an adult partner at each.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to be a station helper.

assessment.method: Observe each child at the six stations and complete the Term 2 record. Record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for each strand: comparing quantity, counting to five, numerals 1 to 5, length and weight, patterns, shapes.

questions.question: What comes next in this pattern?
questions.expected: The next item in the pattern.

lessons.conclusion: Clap for the whole class and sing the closing song. Send the term note home.
lessons.homeConnection: Parents receive a Term 2 note with one strength, one next step and one home idea.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "show Term 2 learning in familiar games and celebrate their work" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
